Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Aether Renewables Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants on the phone line should press * then 1 to ask a question on the phone. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aether Renewables' results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today's call are Mark Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Ellis, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Lena Voss, Chief Technology Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Sustainability Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Emily Chen, Chief Strategy Officer; and David Brooks, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Harlan.

Mark Harlan:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Aether Renewables continues to demonstrate its leadership in the renewable energy sector, achieving a record-breaking performance in the Q2. Our success is a testament to our unwavering commitment to innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence.

Today, I want to highlight eight key aspects of our performance. First, our capital expenditures and operating expenses reflect disciplined execution, with $285 million in CAPEX deployed amid a dynamic landscape, and OPEX at $142 million showing scale efficiencies. Second, capacity factors improved fleet-wide to 38.2%, with solar at 27.8%, wind at 41.6%, and storage utilization at 68.4%. Third, the policy environment, from the U.S. IRA to Europe's REPowerEU, provides strong tailwinds for our pipeline. Fourth, overall highlights include $425 million in revenue up 52% year-over-year, 1.8 GW commissioned, and a $18.7 billion backlog. Fifth, our strategic priorities focus on U.S. execution, global diversification, and tech innovation, with raised FY2024 guidance. Sixth, storage deployments hit 850 MW new capacity, with hybrids now 65% of pipeline. Seventh, gross margins expanded to 28.5% and operating margins to 12.3%, driven by cost efficiencies. Eighth, we secured 1.2 GW in new PPAs at an average $36.50 per MWh.

Now, I'll hand the call over to Sarah Kline to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Mark. Our financial performance in the Q2 was exceptional. Revenue reached $425 million, representing a 52% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 28.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $142 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $85 million, or $0.78 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are significantly raising our full-year guidance for revenue to $1.85-1.95 billion and earnings accordingly.

Let me expand on some of these drivers, starting with our capital expenditures and operating expenses, which highlight our focus on efficiency in a rapidly evolving clean energy market. As a vertically integrated leader in utility-scale solar PV, onshore wind, and battery energy storage systems with over 15 GW of operational assets across North America, Europe, and APAC, our results benefit from U.S. Inflation Reduction Act tailwinds, Europe's REPowerEU, and stabilizing supply chains after polysilicon shortages.

On CAPEX, we invested $285 million this quarter, up 18% year-over-year and aligned with our $1.1 to $1.3 billion annual guide. This supports growth in high-CAGR markets where solar additions are expected at 25% globally, and front-loads spending before 10-15% module price rises from U.S. tariffs on Southeast Asian imports. Solar PV took 62% or $177 million, including the 450 MWdc Desert Bloom project in California's Imperial Valley using Trina Solar HJT bifacial modules at $0.72/W DC, down 8% sequentially, plus 1.2 GW in Texas with Nextracker systems for 15-20% yield gains. Wind was 22% or $63 million for the 300 MW Prairie Winds in Oklahoma with Vestas 15 MW turbines at $1.35 million per MW, unlocking $25 million in IRA 45X credits. BESS and grid integration got 12% or $34 million for 150 MWh LFP from CATL at $120/kWh, supporting four-hour projects under CAISO and FERC rules. R&D took 4% or $11 million for perovskite tandems with Oxford PV and AI digital twins from Siemens Gamesa.

By region, North America saw 65% or $185 million with 40-50% ITC rates, Europe 25% or $71 million despite German grid delays, and APAC 10% with India factory ramp-up against Red Sea logistics hikes. Our portfolio CAPEX efficiency hit $0.85/W versus peers' $0.92/W, via 40% insourced BOS and 70% hedged wafers below $10/kg, targeting 12-15% IRRs and under-8-year paybacks with $40-50/MWh PPA escalators.

Turning to OPEX at $142 million, up only 2% YoY despite 22% portfolio growth to 12.8 GW AC, compressing to 28% of revenue from 32% and cutting LCOE 15% to $32/MWh. Adjusted for insurance resets, it was flat quarter-over-quarter. O&M was 48% or $68 million, with solar at $8/kW-year using AetherAI for 97.8% availability and 25% less downtime, wind at $32/kW-year offset by cheaper new turbines, and BESS under 1% degradation. G&A was 25% or $36 million, down 7% to $2.8/MW with optimized headcount at 1.2 FTEs/100 MW. Land leases and taxes 18% or $26 million at $4.5/kW-year, with Southwest savings. Other 9% or $12 million included carbon credits.

U.S. OPEX led efficiency at $10.5/kW-year, Europe $14/kW-year on labor, APAC $9/kW-year. FY2024 OPEX guided to $580-610 million for 200-300 bps margin gains via robotics and hedges, targeting 55-60% EBITDA margins ahead of peers.

On gross and operating margins, these trends show structural gains across our platform. Non-GAAP gross margin was 28.5%, up 320 bps YoY and 110 bps sequentially, nearing our 27-29% guide, with ex-IRA $24.8% from real efficiencies. Polysilicon dropped 45% to $14/kg, cutting BOM $0.08/W on 23.1% efficient TOPCon modules (85% mix). Texas fab yields hit 98.5%, conversion costs $0.21/W below benchmarks. BESS systems exceeded 35% margins on projects like Gemini Solar + Storage.

U.S. shipments up 55% to 1.8 GW drove 28.5% margins with IRA bonuses, Europe 32% on REPowerEU, APAC 22%. Operating margin hit 12.3%, up 250 bps, with OpEx at 16.2% of revenue via flat R&D at 3.2% for perovskites and SG&A savings. EBITDA margin 18.7%, ROIC 14.2%. We're prioritizing U.S. utility-scale at <3¢/kWh all-in, hedging supplies, and eyeing India's PLI for 30%+ margins. Q4 gross 29-30%, FY 30-32%.

Finally, on new PPAs, we secured over 1.2 GW, lifting backlog to 4.8 GW up 25% YoY. Highlights: 650 MW California hybrid at $38/MWh 15-year with hyperscaler, including 200 MW/800 MWh BESS; 450 MW Texas solar at $32/MWh 12-year with oil & gas; 150 MW UK offshore at $57/MWh equivalent. Last-12-month average $36.50/MWh, down 8% on lower costs but with escalators and hybrids adding 12-15% revenues. U.S. bifurcated $28-42/MWh, Europe resilient, APAC competitive. 65% pipeline de-risked with IG counterparties, Q4 target 800 MW at $35-37/MWh supporting raised FY24 revenue.

I'll now turn the call over to Tom Ellis to discuss our project development activities.

Tom Ellis:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project development pipeline continues to grow rapidly, with 15 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring a substantial number of new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth.

Dr. Lena Voss, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Lena Voss:
Thank you, Tom. We are committed to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing groundbreaking technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will revolutionize the energy landscape.

On capacity factors by technology, our fleet average rose to 38.2% from 35.7% YoY. Solar PV at 27.8%, up 11%, above NREL benchmarks thanks to trackers on 72% new builds, bifacials like LONGi Hi-MO 7, and AI cleaning at Gemini Solar's 32.1%. U.S. 28.5%, Australia 26.3%, Europe retrofits targeting 25%+. Wind at 41.6%, onshore 39.2% with Vestas V150 at Traverse Wind's 43.1%, offshore 54.7% at Borkum Riffgrund. Gains from repowering and software. Storage utilization 68.4%, RTE 92.1%, Hornsdale at 72% stacking revenues. Hybrids boost this, with $800M in long-duration tech for 80%+ in 2025. These drove 14% EBITDA growth, guiding FY2025 to 40-42%.

On storage and hybrids, we added 850 MW BESS to reach 3.2 GW, up 45% YoY, with 92.5% RTE on LFP. Hornsdale-adjacent captured $45M FCAS, Badlands arbitrage IRRs >14%. Hybrids 65% of 12 GW pipeline: California 650 MW solar + 300 MW/1.2 GWh at $42/MWh, Texas 450 MW solar + 200 MW wind + 200 MW/800 MWh, Spain 300 MW solar + 100 MW/400 MWh. Drove 32% Q3 revenue at 42% margins, 4.8 GWh backlog $2.2B. Next-gen iron-air pilots, AI dispatch +18% value. FY24 another 1.2 GW storage, 2 GW hybrids.

Next, Maria Gonzalez will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you, Dr. Voss. Sustainability is deeply ingrained in our corporate culture, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability.

On the policy and regulatory front, the U.S. IRA has spurred $370B investments, with our 12.5 GWdc U.S. pipeline up 28% on 50% ITC stacks, $4.2B uncontracted at $42/MWh vs. $28/MWh LCOE. FAST-41 cut timelines, $450M Arizona expansion for 45X. Southeast booms with FERC reforms. Europe REPowerEU hits 42.5% renewables, German EEG, Spanish agrivoltaics, Portuguese IPCEI hydrogen. CBAM pressures imports, so 65% localized. UK CfD AR6 at £47/MWh. APAC China goals, Australia CIS. PAC $18M advocacy, $2.5B green bonds. Policy capex $1.2T to 2030.

Now, Raj Patel will provide operational highlights.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Maria. Our operational performance remains exceptional. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets. We are implementing best-in-class practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management. We are also investing heavily in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to excel.

Emily Chen, can you provide an update on our strategic initiatives?

Emily Chen:
Thank you, Raj. We are focused on executing our long-term strategic plan, which includes expanding our presence in key markets, diversifying our product offerings, and strengthening our partnerships. We are also actively exploring new opportunities in emerging areas such as green hydrogen and carbon capture.

Our priorities include U.S. pipeline execution on 8 GW for $12B revenue, energizing 1.2 GW Q4 like Desert Bloom, Prairie Hybrid, Mountain View, guiding FY24 $2.4B revenue. FY25 15 GW advancement, $800M capex for 5 GW fab. Global diversification: Europe 1.5 GW offshore FID Q1'25, APAC Vietnam/India 50% revenue growth. Supply hedges 70%. R&D $250M perovskites, solid-state BESS, hydrogen. Q4 $650-700M, FY25 $3.2-3.5B, FCF $700M.

And finally, David Brooks, can you address our risk management strategies?

David Brooks:
Thank you, Emily. We have implemented robust risk management strategies to mitigate potential risks associated with our operations, including market risks, regulatory risks, and environmental risks. We are continuously monitoring and evaluating our risk profile and taking proactive steps to manage these risks effectively.

I'll turn it back to Mark Harlan for closing remarks.

Mark Harlan:
Thank you all. In conclusion, Aether Renewables had a truly exceptional Q2. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our unwavering focus on sustainability will continue to drive long-term growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. Participants, if you would like to ask a question, please press * then 1. To withdraw your question, press * then 2. Please limit to one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from John Smith with GreenInvest Capital. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
What are your plans for investing in new technologies such as green hydrogen?

Dr. Lena Voss:
Thanks for the question, John. Green hydrogen is a key pillar of our multi-vector strategy to deliver firm clean power. We're investing $250 million in R&D this year, including pilots at Texas hybrids producing 50 MW by mid-2025 via PEM electrolyzers paired with solar and BESS. This leverages IRA elective pay for credits and positions us for DOE's $7 billion Hydrogen Hubs. We've secured a 1 GW offtake with Chevron at $1.80/kg, blending with carbon abatement. Internationally, our Portuguese project taps €200 million EU IPCEI funding. Expect 10-15% of FY25 revenue from H2, scaling to 20% by 2027 as LCOE drops below $2/kg with perovskites boosting electrolyzer input efficiency. This de-risks intermittency and opens steel/chemical markets.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with EcoFund Partners. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy market?

Mark Harlan:
Great question, Lisa. Competition is intensifying, but our vertically integrated model—from modules to O&M—gives us a cost edge, with LCOE at $28/MWh versus peers' $32+. We've insourced 40% BOS, hedged 70% supply, and hit 98.5% fab yields for $0.21/W costs. Differentiators like AI-optimized capacity factors (38.2% fleet) and 65% hybrid pipeline secure premium PPAs at $36.50/MWh average. Strategic JVs like Northvolt for sodium-ion and Oxford PV for tandems build moats. With 95% contracted backlog and FAST-41 permitting, we're executing faster. We'll maintain 25%+ CAGR by focusing on U.S. IRA sweet spots and APAC localization, outpacing pure developers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with SustainEnergy Advisors. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Can you discuss the potential impact of climate change on your operations?

David Brooks:
Thanks, Mike. Climate change poses risks like extreme weather, but our strategies mitigate them proactively. We've modeled scenarios per TCFD, stress-testing for hurricanes (post-Idalia insurance resets) and droughts affecting hydro-interties. Assets feature hail-resistant tilting, thermal-managed BESS (<1% degradation), and drone inspections cutting downtime 25%. Diversified siting—U.S. Southwest DNI stability, North Sea winds—balances exposures. Sustainability goals cut Scope 1/2 emissions 40% by 2025 via electrification. REC portfolio monetizes 5.2M tons CO2e. Upside: warmer winds boost offshore CF to 54.7%. Insurance covers 90%, reserves $50M. Overall, net positive as we supply resilient clean energy.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with RenewTech Ventures. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
What are your expectations for the long-term profitability of your renewable energy projects?

Sarah Kline:
Excellent point, Sarah. Long-term profitability is robust, with new builds targeting 12-15% IRRs and <8-year paybacks on $40-50/MWh escalator PPAs. Backlog at $18.7B through 2028, 95% contracted at $36.50/MWh average, yields 42% EBITDA margins expanding to 55-60%. Hybrids stack revenues: energy 45%, capacity 30%, ancillary 25%. LCOE $25-28/MWh unsubsidized, beating gas by 40%. IRA/PTC/ITC at 50-60% effective, transferability de-risks. O&M efficiencies to $8/kW-year solar, utilization 72%+. FY25 FCF $700M supports ROIC 12-14%, dividends $0.20/share. In $1.7T market, our 25 GW pipeline ensures 20%+ EPS CAGR.

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Mark Harlan for any closing remarks.

Mark Harlan:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Aether Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
